subject: PrivNet heartbeat suppression — escalation, bridge call, and follow-up
messages:
From: Medivault Oncall <oncall@medivault.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: ellen.singh@medivault.com, t.wallace@medivault.com
Date: 2026-12-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: [URGENT] PrivNet agents not checking in — us-west-2

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing a heartbeat suppression event against our Private/VPC deployment (cluster medivault-prod, us-west-2) at ~08:55 PST. Multiple inference agents stopped checking in to the control plane; customer traffic started queueing and a small percentage of requests returned 503. Impacting a subset of production routes (~12%).

We are attaching the on-host systemd logs we captured. Can you confirm this is a Redwood control-plane/connectivity issue or something local to our network? We're preparing to open a formal outage on our side but wanted to get your OOB confirmation first.

Attachments: privnet_debug_log.tar.gz

Thanks,
Medivault Oncall
[Attachment: privnet_debug_log.tar.gz (application/gzip)]

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Medivault Oncall <oncall@medivault.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: [URGENT] PrivNet agents not checking in — us-west-2

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Ellen/Toby — we see the same symptom on our monitoring (control-plane heartbeat suppression metric spiking). I'm standing up a bridge now and pulling the on-call infra team in.

Planned immediate actions:
- Start a debug bridge (10m) to gather sanity logs and confirm whether the control plane is accepting connections.
- If control-plane is reachable, we'll target an incremental rollback of the last agent rollout.
- If unreachable, we'll trigger the fallback routing policy to route traffic to hosted-compatible model variants to reduce customer impact.

Joining bridge: https://zoom.redwood.com/privnet-bridge-9347 (bridges invite sent separately).

I'll loop back with a short timeline in 15m.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[jasmine@redwood.com]

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:26:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivNet agents not checking in — preliminary findings

On initial triage: I see an automated upgrade job (privnet-agent-20261206-qtz) that completed around 02:18 UTC (earlier night) which changed the agent's conntrack/iptables preflight handling. After the upgrade, our controlplane health-checks observed a burst of connection resets followed by the new agent instances setting their heartbeat TTL to a lower threshold. The controlplane's suppression circuit-breaker was triggered when the TTLs drifted below the configured 30s window.

Commands run:
- journalctl -u privnet-agent.service --since "2026-12-06 02:00" | tail -n 120
  -> repeated: "heartbeat expired; last-seen 00:00:34"
- /opt/redwood/bin/agent --dump-config
  -> shows: heartbeat_ttl: 22s (expected 60s in stable channel)

Hypothesis: a packaging mistake pushed a debug/default config (heartbeat_ttl=22s) to the rollout. That combined with a transient network jitter caused the suppression cascade.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) push a quick config patch to set heartbeat_ttl back to 60s and restart agents in a rolling fashion (low blast radius).
2) if restart risks prolonged downtime, trigger controlplane to temporarily relax suppression thresholds for medivault-prod while we remediate.

I'll prepare a config patch and test on a canary host. Attaching runbook-diff.txt with the proposed one-line change.

— Aditya (oncall infra)
[Attachment: runbook-diff.txt (text)]

From: Ellen Singh <ellen.singh@medivault.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Toby Wallace <t.wallace@medivault.com>, oncall@medivault.com
Date: 2026-12-07T09:41:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivNet agents not checking in — impact details

Thanks Jasmine/Aditya. Our SREs confirm that 14% of production requests to the real-time route are seeing 503s or 1-2s tail latency increases while the queue absorbs the retry load. We are seeing a small increase in user-facing errors (customer-visible).

Please prioritize the minimum-risk path. If you need us to flip a routing flag or accept a short restart window, we can coordinate immediately. We need to understand expected time to mitigation and whether this will affect our run-rate billing.

— Ellen
Ellen Singh
Head of SRE, Medivault
ellen.singh@medivault.com

Date: 2026-12-07T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: PrivNet agents not checking in — mitigation and next steps

Ellen/Toby — thank you. Quick update and plan: we validated Aditya's hypothesis on a canary and will take path (1) with a conservative rollout:

- 10:10 UTC: push heartbeat_ttl patch (22s -> 60s) to canary node and restart agent (observed stabilization).
- 10:20 UTC: rollout to remaining agent hosts in medivault-prod in 5-host batches with watch windows.
- 10:42 UTC: suppression metric returned to normal; queue drained; customer 503s fell back to baseline.

We will also publish a post-incident RCA with artifact links (logs, canary run, packaging checks). As a precaution, we're adding a gating check to the agent packaging pipeline to prevent heartbeat overrides in the stable channel.

Estimate to full remediation: complete by 10:45 UTC. We will coordinate any billing/credits separately with your finance team — happy to expedite.

Attaching snapshot from the bridge (screenshot-bridgecall.png) and the debug tar you sent (we appended additional controlplane logs).

— Jasmine
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: privnet_debug_log.tar.gz (application/gzip)]

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Singh <ellen.singh@medivault.com>, jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T16:42:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: PrivNet heartbeat suppression — RCA and next steps

Ellen/Toby — following up with the formal RCA and next steps (summary here; full report + artifacts in linked Drive):

Summary (short):
- Root cause: an automated packaging/regression accidentally set heartbeat_ttl=22s for the agent in the stable rollout channel during the Dec 6 upgrade. The reduced TTL combined with transient network jitter triggered the control-plane suppression circuit (suppression window < configured threshold).
- Impact window: 2026-12-07 08:55 — 2026-12-07 10:42 UTC (approx).
- Customer impact: up to 14% of requests on the real-time route experienced 503s or elevated tail latency while queues drained.

Remediations completed:
- Reverted configuration to heartbeat_ttl=60s and performed a rolling restart with watch windows.
- Added a packaging gate in CI that prevents heartbeat overrides in the stable channel (INFRA-PR-1942).
- Added alerting to detect TTL drift separately from agent heartbeats to reduce suppression cascades.

Attachments & artifacts: privnet_debug_log.tar.gz; runbook-diff.txt; screenshot-bridgecall.png. Full logs and the RCA doc are available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrivNet/medivault-incident-9347

We're open to a follow-up call with your SRE/finance teams to discuss credits and any contractual concerns. We've flagged this incident for a severity review and will share the final postmortem within 3 business days.

Apologies for the disruption — please let me know if you'd like us to schedule a technical walkthrough.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
[Attachment: runbook-diff.txt (text)]
